predecessors.name: Marinid Sultanate
predecessors.text: the former Marinid realm: after the 1465 revolt at Fez 'the Wattasids eventually established control over the former Marinid realm' (only its north in practice)

successors.name: Saadi Sultanate
successors.text: Fez and the north, taken by the Saadians on 28 January 1549 and finally in September 1554

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Yahya (Abu Abd Allah al-Sheikh)
Muhammad al-Burtuqali (Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad)
Nasir ad-Din al-Qasri Muhammad ibn Ahmad
Ahmad ibn Muhammad (Abu al-Abbas), second reign
Ali Abu Hassun (Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad)

ledger.x: 1472: Muhammad ibn Yahya establishes the Wattasid sultanate at Fez.
1508: Spain holds the Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera.
1554: Ali Abu Hassun briefly retakes Fez.
September 1554: the Saadians retake Fez and end the Wattasids.
1554: the Wattasid dynasty is supplanted by the Saadis.

wars.name: Wattasid attempts on Asilah and Tangier
wars.outcome: Failed: the Wattasid side 'attempted to capture Asilah and Tangier in 1508, 1511 and 1515, but without success'; both stayed Portuguese.

wars.name: Saadi conquest of the Wattasid realm
wars.outcome: The Saadians seized Marrakesh in 1524 (or 1525), partitioned Morocco 'roughly along the Oum Er-Rbia River' in the 1527 Treaty of Tadla, took Fez on 28 January 1549, lost it to the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun in January 1554 and retook it in September 1554.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on the pages except the roughly drawn Oum Er-Rbia partition of 1527; the northern realm's edges, the Zayyanid frontier in the east and the Portuguese coastal enclaves are all approximate.
